beats.t: The clock tower's back entrance was shabbier than expected. A rusty lift rope hung beside a narrow door barely wide enough for a bread basket.
My sister sends bread down here every morning before dawn. Breakfast for the vault guards.
Thanks to Miss Luna, we can skip seven layers of front doors. You're today's star contributor.
Then do I get five stars?
Five stars and a flower stamp. Let's tell your sister when she wakes up.
At the far end of the square, a lantern swayed. A rabbit patrol in a blue uniform passed by, yawning.
Get down. The patrol comes around on the hour. Four minutes until the next one.
(Four minutes. On this island, that's a roll and a half.)
Look at that patrol rabbit's ears. They're twitching at the smell of skewers. That one's hungry, too.
Once the patrol turned the corner, the four darted from shadow to shadow. Luna led the way and lifted the narrow door's bolt.
The lift basket creaked downward. One after another, the four and Luna clung to the rope and slid into darkness.
The first level was a factory. Hundreds of people worked machines in silence. Instead of coins, ticking grains of sand poured from them.
Are these all guards? They look more like workers.
This is the level where people work off the time they owe. Their days don't pass while they work here. But they can't go home, either.
Every worker's face was blurred. Some were children, others elderly. Among the indistinct faces, one large panda struggled to stay awake.
They all look hungry. Faces that have lost their taste.
Change of plan. I'm feeding them, not luring them. The scent diversion is a bonus.
Moka lit his portable brazier. Twenty spicy skewers sizzled at once, stirring the factory air.
One by one, the machines fell silent. The workers raised their heads. The sound of swallowing spread among the blurred faces.
Line up. No charge. But if it's good, tell me it's good. That's your payment.
The panda took the first skewer. With one bite, the blurred edges of its eyes briefly cleared. Delicious, it said in the smallest voice.
Did you hear? It's delicious!
Of course. This time, the flavor is real.
A small child stood at the end of the skewer line, a baby rabbit with folded ears. Even after receiving a skewer, the child only stared at their wrist without eating.
Not eating? It's good.
The child held out a wrist. Tiny numbers blinked on it. Debt remaining before home: 00:01:00.
One minute? You're here because of one minute?
The child nodded. Just one more minute of work, and they could go to their mother, they said softly through the smell of skewers.
(One minute. With the twelve I earned...)
Not now, my lady. That's the price of the seventh chamber's door. We'll see them again on the way back.
Wait for me. I'll make sure to stop here on our way back. Eat your skewer before it gets cold.
It smells like my sister's bread. A warm smell.
We go down while Moka keeps their attention. Time slows from the second level onward.
Miss Luna, stay beside Moka. The grown-ups will go below.
No. It's my sister's day. I'm going to find it.
Then come with us as far as the third level. Wait there, and I'll bring it back for you. I promise.
The second level. A golden corridor stretched on endlessly. Needles on the gauges set into the walls moved as slowly as honey.
After one step, Yeoni's feet grew heavy. At the second, their own heartbeat thundered in their ears.
My breath... it's rising.
Support it. Like yesterday. Set it down low.
Yeoni sent their breath below their belly. The severed sprout behind their ear stirred slightly. Their legs moved again.
Before the third-level door, the corridor jolted. Floor panels flipped, and metal arms shot upward. A silent trap, without even an alarm.
Yeongnyangi sprang forward. His golden claws cut three metal arms in one stroke. The severed arms fell slowly through the slowed time.
The way's clear. You need to open that door.
Yes, yes. I'll eat the locked parts.
Yundal pressed his palm to the door handle. The whole lock disappeared into the hole. His shoulders twitched once.
Locks on this island taste strongly of iron. Makes my teeth ache.
Mister, it got bigger again just now, didn't it? Let me see your hand.
It might hurt less if a lady held my hand.
Say things like that when your hand isn't hurting!
They parted with Luna on the third level. She crouched by the door and spread five fingers. Come back within five hours.
The fourth, fifth, and sixth levels. Time thickened as they descended. Falling drops of water hung suspended like pearls.
I think I'm going to sneeze.
Do it now, and that's a week.
I know. That's why I'm holding it in. This level gets one star.
Moka's nose twitched. Without a word, Yeongnyangi covered it with the hem of his cloak. The sneeze vanished quietly into the star-embroidered lining.
Your cloak has a sneeze filter, too, Yeongnyangi? One extra star.
Free of charge. Today only.
The seventh chamber. A vast circular vault stood open. Thousands of hourglasses lined the walls in tier upon tier.
Is every one of these someone's day?
A day, a month, ten years. Time sold and stolen on this island.
Each hourglass made a tiny sound. A child's laughter, rice cooking, someone calling a name. The sounds of days that had been sold.
All these sounds have flavor. Sounds like the smell of dinner in someone's home.
Don't listen too long. Follow someone else's day, and you could find yourself stuck in it.
[ Luna's sister · Today remaining: 01:12:40 ]
Yeoni searched the labels one by one. At the end of the third row, they found an hourglass bearing a drawing of flour-covered hands.
Found it! Hers! It has a picture of hands!
Yundal ran to the opposite wall. One drawer at the very bottom had a blank label instead of a name. The drawer was empty.
It's gone. The place where my birth hour should be.
Mister...
It's all right. That rabbit must carry it around. The type that gets attached to things it's eaten.
Then came the sound of a page turning in the center of the vault. Very slowly, very deliberately.
A black tiger sat on a round dais at the vault's center. A ledger lay open over its cloak, and a golden egg rested at its feet.
You're late, pig. Though I knew you'd take the bakery lift.
You knew, and you didn't stop us?
No vault keeper stops guests coming in. It stops them leaving.
The tiger turned a page. Yeoni saw it clearly. Among the densely filled lines, only one was empty.
[ Flower Pig · Uncollected ]
I was told to collect your time on the next island. But you've walked right into the vault yourself.
Who told you that? Is your boss in that ledger, too?
So many questions. Leave a debt alone, and it grows. That's why you collect on time.
Then what about you? What did you borrow, and from whom?
The tiger's tail stopped. Its page-turning paw hung in the air for the briefest moment.
Nothing a pig needs to know.
(Just now, it couldn't answer.)
Keep your paws off Yeoni.
Stay out of it, cat. You're already cracked, too. That left paw.
Yeongnyangi's left front paw twitched almost imperceptibly. Yeoni missed it. Their eyes were on the egg at the tiger's feet.
(That egg... why does it seem so familiar? It's like something inside me is calling.)
My lady, that egg. 辰, Chen. The character for your Hour Branch. Chen Earth is a storehouse. This entire vault was built on that egg.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ? ]
Why is my character buried under a vault?
As though it recognized Yeoni, the egg trembled very slightly. Something stirred beneath its golden shell.
A chart with an empty hour is a house with its storehouse left open. Anyone can come in and stack things inside.
You're talking too much. Give me the egg. And give her day back.
The tiger swept its tail once. Black water spread along the clock hands on the floor. The moment it touched an ankle, it froze time.
Don't touch the water! Touch it, and you'll stop!
Yeongnyangi drew out a golden line and split the flow. Through the opening, Moka leaped and clutched Luna's sister's hourglass to his chest.
Got it! Hers! I've got it right here!
Take that one. It wasn't in my ledger to begin with. It belongs to the rabbit's share.
Then I'll take that egg, too.
That, you may not.
Yeoni leaped onto the dais. The instant their hoof touched the egg, the entire dais became a giant clock face.
A bell rang seven times. The clock hands spun around Yeoni, and transparent glass walls rose around their body.
I can't move! My breath... I can't get my breath down!
[ Time trap · Escape price: 72:00:00  Held: 71:53:09  Shortfall: 00:06:51 ]
Yeoni.
I won't say I'm sorry. There's no column for that in the ledger.
Beyond the glass, two blue ears dropped from a vent in the vault ceiling. Blue Rabbit hung upside down and waved.
Oh my! You're exactly six minutes and fifty-one seconds short. Shall Blue Rabbit Finance lend it to you? Just a teeny-tiny bit of interest!
(Borrow, and I get out. Refuse, and I stop here.)
